Facing the future of web development, relying on a solid foundation
Ready to expand the capabilities of your web development framework? WebForms Core version 1.9 is not just an update, but a significant step forward in the evolution of the platform. By strengthening the connection between server-side and front-end development, this release empowers you to create modern web applications with unique and innovative features. In this release, WebForms Core has reached a new level of maturity and stability. With full support for async and sync patterns in different situations, developers are given more flexibility and control. This feature is the result of months of hard work and research by the development team, and is now available to you in a fully tested and proven form in WebForms Core. With the introduction of Transient DOM, DOM changes are applied seamlessly and without any flickering. This architecture, using optimization concepts, brings you a very smooth and efficient experience similar to that seen in modern frameworks like React and Vue, in the rich and mature environment of WebForms. Version 1.9 not only addresses the complex needs of today’s developers, but also showcases the maturity, flexibility, and power of WebForms Core as a complete, all-in-one platform. Today, WebForms Core is not just a server-side tool; it is a comprehensive platform for building single-page applications (SPAs), managing state, interacting with WASM, and implementing RESTful architectures. All these new features and capabilities are automatically and very easily available to the developer, and there is no need for complex configurations and a lot of programming code to use the features of this new version. In the next few days, a new version of WebForms Core technology will be presented, as well as a new version of the CodeBehind framework, and we will fully discuss the new features and capabilities of these two.

entry.title: Checking Out of Winter - irisCTF
Will AI Agents Kill Coding—or Make Us 10x Developers?
entry.summary: Introduction AI has gone way beyond autocomplete. With agentic AI models now capable of writing code, testing it, and even deploying applications, developers everywhere are asking: Do we still need to write code ourselves? Some predict the death of coding as a profession, while others believe AI will make developers 10x more productive. Let’s explore both sides. The Case for "AI Will Replace Coders" 1. Agents can already complete tasks 2. No-code + AI convergence 3. Economics favor automation The Case for "AI Will Empower Coders" 1. Oversight remains essential 2. Complexity needs human reasoning 3. History repeats itself What Developers Are Experiencing Pro-AI: Some teams report cutting sprint timelines in half using Copilot Agents or GPT-powered assistants. Skeptical: Others find AI-generated code harder to maintain, leading to more bugs later. Reality: It depends on whether AI is treated as a junior dev or as the entire dev team. How to Future-Proof Yourself Instead of worrying, focus on skills AI can’t easily replace: AI Collaboration Skills → Learn how to prompt, guide, and review AI effectively. System Design & Architecture → Think beyond code; design scalable systems. Agentic Workflows → Experiment with AI as “your dev team,” not just a tool. Conclusion: The 10x Future AI won’t kill coding. It will kill the way we code today. The best developers won’t be the ones who write the most lines of code. They’ll be the ones who can leverage AI to deliver value faster, cleaner, and smarter. So the question isn’t: Will AI replace developers? Will you adapt and become a 10x AI-powered developer?
